notes.text: Greek housing demand has been financed largely without new mortgage credit: net mortgage flows only turned positive in October 2025 after years of deleveraging, and annual housing loan growth was just 1.1% in February 2026. With equity and foreign capital doing most of the work, policy-rate cuts reach prices mainly through a slow revival of lending, even as the average rate on new loans fixed for up to five years fell to 2.95% in February 2026.

sources.title: Mortgage rates in Greece hit nine-year low as lending rebounds

notes.text: Since 1 January 2025 binding Bank of Greece limits cap loan-to-value at origination at 90% for first-time buyers and 80% for other buyers, and debt service at 50% and 40% of disposable income respectively, with lenders able to exempt 10% of new loans each quarter from each cap. The limits were set pre-emptively against credit growth while mortgage lending was still contracting, so they act as a guardrail on the coming credit recovery rather than a current brake on prices.

notes.text: Under Law 5100/2024 the golden visa minimum property investment rose to EUR 800,000 in Attica, the Thessaloniki area, Mykonos, Santorini and islands above 3,100 inhabitants, and to EUR 400,000 elsewhere, with a 120 square metre minimum size and a ban on short-term letting of qualifying property. Transactions from 1 September 2024 must comply; the EUR 250,000 route survives only for conversions of non-residential buildings, which steers foreign capital away from the tight urban resale stock.

sources.title: Understanding the new Golden Visa law no. 5100/2024: key points and implications

notes.text: Since January 2025 the authorities have stopped issuing new short-term rental registration numbers in Athens' first, second and third municipal districts, and in June 2025 the freeze was extended to at least the end of 2026 on the grounds that affordable long-term housing in the centre is scarce. Existing registrations continue, so the measure caps further conversion of central flats to tourist use rather than returning stock to the long-term market.

sources.title: Athens extends ban on new short-term rentals in city center until 2026

notes.text: The Spiti mou II programme, funded with EUR 2 billion from the Recovery and Resilience Facility through the Hellenic Development Bank, finances first-home purchases for households within set income limits; by November 2025 over 11,000 people had been housed and income ceilings were raised to EUR 25,000 for single applicants. Loan contracts had to be signed by 31 August 2026, so the demand boost to the lower end of the market is likely to fade unless the scheme is renewed.

sources.title: My Home II: higher income limits and extended deadlines

notes.text: The Bank of Greece price indices are built from valuations that all credit institutions report on properties they appraise, about 957,800 valuations to end-2025, rather than from registered transaction prices. Apartment indices are published quarterly for Athens, Thessaloniki, other cities and other areas, split into new (up to five years old) and older flats, so they measure appraised values rather than achieved sale prices.
